band_dissents.reasoning: 35% for five consecutive years compounds FY26 FCF of $96.68B to $433.5B by Y5 — roughly 4.5x — on a base that is already the largest FCF pool in the market. The engine derives 35% by capping trailing fcf_yoy of 58.9%, but that trailing rate was itself flattered by a working-capital-light, one-off step change: FCF conversion is only 80.5% of net income and slipping, capex dollars nearly doubled ($3.24B to $6.04B), and gross margin gave back 392bp in FY26. A 22-32% five-year band still embeds hyperscale-buildout leadership without extrapolating a once-in-a-cycle demand shock at constant rate; note the top of my range is only modestly below the default, so this is a trim, not a reversal.

band_dissents.reasoning: The engine takes g_high=14.9% from FY25 fcf_yoy, but that year was an unusually strong one (revenue +13.7% with R&D essentially flat). The nine-month FY26 evidence points the other way: fcf__current_quarter of $6.83B cumulative against fcf__current_annual of $12.82B, with capex_pct_revenue__current_quarter at 4.8% versus 2.7% at the annual mark. Compounding 14.9% for five years from a base that is currently shrinking is not defensible; low-single-digit growth over the explicit period (0-4%) reflects Apple modem attrition plus a possible China Android trough recovery.

band_dissents.reasoning: The engine's 15.8% high-growth rate is FY26 FCF growth, which was driven by FCF margin expanding to 34.7% from 32.8% off a restructuring trough — a lever now largely pulled, since FCF margin (34.7%) has effectively converged with the guided non-GAAP operating margin. Revenue grew 9.6% and FY27 guidance implies ~10-11%; with capex already at only 1.4% of revenue there is minimal remaining conversion headroom, so forward FCF growth should track revenue growth, not the 15.8% margin-catch-up rate. Additionally, the new ~$39.3B debt stack introduces a permanent annual interest claim on FCF that did not exist in the FY26 base, arguing for the low end of the range.
